Second arithmetic term for the gcd in base $5$

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural numbers, at least one of them greater than $1$, and let $s_{a,b}$ be the gcd-term sequence. For every natural number $n$, $s_{a,b}(n) \le s_{1,1}(n) = n + 1$, and $s_{a,b}(n) = s_{1,1}(n)$ only if $n = 0$.
nodes.title: The gcd-term sequence is bounded by $n + 1$

nodes.summary: Let $a, b \ge 1$ be natural numbers and let $s_{a,b}$ be the gcd-term sequence. Every value $s_{a,b}(n)$ is a natural number, and $s_{a,b}(ab) = \gcd(a, b) + 1$.
nodes.title: The gcd-term sequence is integral and recovers the gcd

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a, b \ge 1$, the gcd-term sequence satisfies $s_{a,b}(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: Initial value of the gcd-term sequence

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $n$, $s_{a,b}(n)$ is the rational number that is the coefficient of $z^n$ in the inverse of the formal power series $(z^a - 1)(z^b - 1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. For $a, b \ge 1$ this series has constant coefficient $1$, so $s_{a,b}$ is the coefficient sequence of $f_{a,b}(z) = 1 / ((z^a - 1)(z^b - 1))$.
